## Failing lines

### F-1 — the successor path of `mint` writes an `Identity` whose kind and arena need not match its address

`mint.ts` 165 – 167: when a record carries `address` (handed on by M0-d-05b's succession), `natural = id = rec.address`.
The record's `kind` is never checked: `checkKind` runs only inside `addressOf` / `userAddressOf`, on the natural path.
The handed-on address's `kind:` prefix and arena prefix are never compared with the record's `kind` and `key.arena`.
Probes on the built package (`scratchpad/check05a/probe.mjs`; `x = addressOf('plot', lineageHash(key(0)))`, a retired
live entry at `x`):

```
P1 malformed kind + handed-on address: ok -> {"id":"plot:3p7t2a00nw1xg","kind":"pl ot","key":{"layer":"ground","part":0},…}
P1b malformed kind, no hand-on (control): threw RangeError: address: not an entity kind: pl ot
P2 kind mismatch (building handed plot:): ok -> {"id":"plot:3p7t2a00nw1xg","kind":"building","key":{"layer":"ground","part":0},…}
P2b arena mismatch (sky2 record handed a ground address): ok -> {"id":"plot:3p7t2a00nw1xg","kind":"plot","key":{"layer":"sky","part":2},…}
```

The design clauses this breaks are both in the item's `sections`. §6.3's `EntityKind`: "a type of §2.8's entity
registry, as `Identity.kind` and an address's `kind:` prefix spell it". §6.3's matching hands an address only to "the
fresh entity with the same kind". §2.1 *Ids*: an address is "prefixed with its arena outside the ground layer". Every
handed-on test in `mint.test.ts` (lines 108 – 127, 148 – 154) uses kind `plot` on ground part 0. So a mint that
accepts a mismatch passes the whole suite. C-0179 (4)'s refusals ("a malformed field") and its own rule — the mint
already refuses a survivor's or a doubly handed address — show the seat meant the succession path to be guarded.

**Required change** (`mint.ts`, `mint.test.ts`):

- **(a)** Check every record's `kind` with the kind rule, whether or not it carries an address.
- **(b)** Refuse (RangeError) a handed-on address whose `parseAddress` kind differs from the record's `kind`.
- **(c)** Refuse a handed-on address whose prefix does not name the record's arena: the layer always, and the part off
  the ground layer. A ground address of any part is bare. If the seat reads a case where a successor's address keeps
  another arena's prefix, it records that case instead in a new choices row naming §2.1 and the test.
- Add the three cases (P1, P2, P2b) as refusal tests.

### F-2 — `mint` does not refuse a malformed `live` lineage or seed key, so a signed-lane survivor defeats the dup rule

`mint.ts` 121 – 125 adds every live entry's `lineage` to the hash set with no check. `checkSeedKey` (89 – 91) checks
only the length. The seed key's lanes are checked by the kernel's `entityKey`, which never runs on an empty batch.
C-0179 (4) states "Refused (RangeError): … a malformed field". The receipts (`probe3.mjs`, `probe.mjs`):

```
fresh hash [ 3406433389, 2266701542 ] survivor lineage as an Int32Array gives [ -888533907, -2028265754 ]
survivor as u32 lanes -> dup 1 | survivor as signed lanes -> dup 0 (no refusal; the fresh entity shares the survivor's draws: true )
P4 live lineage [1]: ok -> "plot:3p7t2a00nw1xg"
P4c seed key non-u32, empty batch: ok -> []
```

The first pair is the hazard §6.3's dup rule exists to stop ("so no two live entities share draws"). Any caller that
holds lineage words in an `Int32Array` hands the survivor's hash in signed form. The mint then silently mints a second
live entity on the survivor's streams. The test "refuses … a malformed seed key" covers only a seed key of length 3.

**Required change** (`mint.ts`, `mint.test.ts`):

- Refuse a live entry whose `lineage` is not two u32 lanes, or whose `id` is not a string, and a tombstone whose `id`
  is not a string.
- Check the seed key's four lanes as u32 before reading the batch.
- Test the signed-lane survivor, a `[1]` lineage and `[1, 2, 3, 1.5]` with an empty batch.
- Alternatively, narrow C-0179 (4)'s wording by a new row. But the signed-lane survivor still needs the refusal,
  because without it the dup rule's promise fails silently.

**Fix lane:** `build/M0-d-05a-fix1`, editing `packages/model/src/identity/mint.ts` and
`packages/model/test/identity/mint.test.ts` only (plus a choices row if F-1 (c)'s alternative is taken). The fix round
re-runs F-1 and F-2 and the item's whole test set.

## Notes (no fix asked of this item)

* **N-1 (for M0-m-01 / the session).** `model/test/types/types.test.ts`'s reflection test builds a TypeScript program
  under vitest's default 5 s limit. It timed out twice on this shared 4-CPU container (6846 ms, 5535 ms). It passed in
  the whole-workspace run, and it passed with only the limit raised (7573 ms at load average 11.42). An explicit limit on that one test would stop it flaking while seats share the machine. The
  identity folder adds four small files to a program that already read `@plat/kernel` (`model/src/types/kernel.ts` 47).
* **N-2 (for the session, carried from `checks/M0-d-01.md` N8 / N16).** `M0-work.json`'s M0-d-05a still lists
  `"choices": []`. C-0147 and C-0179 hold this item, and its `tests` do not name the entity-key cache. The item honours
  both rows anyway; routing them into the twin belongs to a spec lane.
* **N-3 (PLAUSIBLE, no change asked).** `parseAddress` accepts any token text without `:`, `/` or whitespace
  (`plot:abc`, `plot:ABC`, `plot:abc~`, `plot:~1`, `plot:abc~x~y`; probe P3), and `address.test.ts` 115 – 118 asserts
  short tokens on purpose. Opacity and the design's other address forms (a plan part's `room:` addresses resolve
  through their building) make a lenient token a defensible reading of C-0179 (3)'s "token". A later round may state
  that in the row.
* **N-4 (information for M0-x-02).** `@plat/model` exports `TOWN_ROOT` (the lineage key) and `@plat/site` exports
  `TOWN_ROOT` (handle 0). C-0179 (6) declares them as two things. A module that imports both needs an alias.
* **N-5 (information for M0-d-05b).** `mint` takes a handed-on address only from a `retired` live entry. Succession
  must mark the re-derived set `retired: true` in `live` and hand each old address to at most one record. After F-1,
  it must also hand each address to a record of the same kind and arena.
